events.note: Imported from the legacy dossier: research verdict 'ready', tier T2 (tool-corroborated), researchedAt 2026-09-24. The verdict and tier are re-expressed as research.state and an evidence class; no product status is carried.

Legacy contract review text for 'twilio-api-key-secret' (verbatim legacy text; the date is the dossier researchedAt, not the authoring date): Twilio documents the API Key Secret's functional role but no character-class grammar. The bare 32-character alphanumeric shape, gated on a same-line API Key SID or the word "twilio", is corroborated by TruffleHog's twilioapikey detector; gitleaks's twilio-api-key rule instead targets the SK-prefixed SID, not this bare secret.

Evidence review for issue 70 (2026-10-03, automation, not independently reviewed). Of the 6 fixtures held at legacy T2: twilio--twilio-api-key-secret-request-signature-encoded-value is re-based from project-policy to provider-documented (Twilio documents the X-Twilio-Signature header as an HMAC-SHA1 signature keyed with the auth token; role of the value only). The other 5 stay project-policy: account-sid-public-id and api-key-sid-public-id (Twilio's secure-credentials page names the Account SID next to the Auth Token as credentials to protect, and its key resource page says Twilio uses the key sid and secret as the credentials; CredSweeper's 'Twilio Credentials' rule and detect-secrets treat AC and SK ids as findings and gitleaks, Nosey Parker and betterleaks flag the SK id, so no two artifacts are consistent with silence and no provider page says these ids are public); missing-identifier and short-secret (Twilio documents no length or alphabet for an API Key Secret; only the TruffleHog twilioapikey detector requires a 32-character secret beside an SK id, one artifact; short-secret also holds an SK id); wrong-companion-near-miss (same SK/AC ids, no provider statement on the secret format). Searched: Twilio docs (glossary SID, key resource v1, API keys overview, create keys in Console, usage API, secure credentials, webhooks security, E.164, auth token REST), twilio-oai iam v1 spec, Twilio CLI and Serverless Toolkit validation code, and the Twilio rules of gitleaks, betterleaks, Nosey Parker, detect-secrets, CredSweeper, TruffleHog and Kingfisher (Kingfisher's Twilio rule is generated from betterleaks); osv-scalibr has none. Not restorable on present evidence for those 5.
